short: The last of Augustus's line, whose descent into extravagance and purges ended in the empire's first civil war.
full:
Nero became emperor at sixteen on 13 October 54 CE, guided at first by his mother Agrippina, the philosopher Seneca, and the praetorian prefect Burrus. Early years of relatively sound government gave way after Agrippina's murder in 59 CE to increasingly erratic rule: the purge of the Senate, the killing of his wife Octavia, and, after the great fire of Rome in 64 CE, the persecution of a suspect scapegoat community.

Provincial revolts in Gaul and Spain in 68 CE, combined with the defection of the Praetorian Guard, left Nero without support. He fled Rome and took his own life on 9 June 68 CE, the last emperor of the Julio-Claudian dynasty founded by Augustus. His death, with no designated heir, opened a year of civil war among rival claimants for the throne.
